items.author: levie
items.text:
Correct take. 99% of tokens in the world will get consumed in an enterprise context. 

They will be for writing code, combing through insane amounts of life sciences research, automating manufacturing, securing enterprises, detecting fraud, and thousands of other tasks like this that have significant economic value. This is both where the cost of AI can be most justified but also where the impact of parallel workers doing tasks on your behalf is most useful.

Even the agents that most impact consumers will often be wrapped up as just end to end services where the consumer doesn’t think about there being an AI system on the other end, like faster insurance or onboarding to a bank.

The key though is it’s going to take years for diffusion of agents across the economy because workflows have to re-engineered to incorporate AI, which is a complete change to how most work happens today. Anyone who’s expecting this to happen overnight should be updating their timelines.

quoted_tweet.author: infinitefun_
quoted_tweet.name: sean lee
quoted_tweet.text:
yeah, no.

the average consumer has a near zero need for offloading cognitive work. what they need is their netflix and their doordash — your job as a consumer is literally to chill tf out and stay happy and motivated 

if you dont intuit this as obvious you're most likely neck-deep in a muck of motivated reasoning as a consumer founder / VC
 
okay you can use agents to search the web and synthesize findings on what to buy. okay you have cognitive chores like filing tax returns and sifting thru email. sounds like great features to bake into google and gmail!

on the other hand, your job as a knowledge worker is to convert your cognition into something of economic value — and then because of competitive market dynamics, you'll also need all the cognitive amplification that's available on the market.

the biggest problems need the most cognition. the consumer takes care of problems scoped to themselves. the knowledge workers together take care problems concerning society.

when we look back, we'll remember how AI agents helped us cure cancer, not how your agent helped you order pizza over imessage.

items.title: Levie：全球 99% token 将消耗在企业场景，agent 扩散仍需数年
items.summary: Aaron Levie 认为全球绝大多数 token 会消耗在企业语境：写代码、梳理生命科学研究、制造自动化、安全与反欺诈等有明确经济价值的任务。企业场景最能证明 AI 成本合理性，也最适合并行 agent 代劳。即便影响消费者的 agent，也常被包装成端到端服务（如更快保险/开户），用户未必感知背后有 AI。关键约束是：工作流需要改造，agent 在经济中的扩散仍需数年。
items.recommend_reason: 用“token 消耗结构 + 扩散时滞”给企业 AI 叙事定锚，避免只盯 C 端聊天。

items.author: IndieDevHailey
items.text:
Codex 用户都懂，经常被“剩余额度”支配：
平时怕额度放着不用白白浪费，真正想做项目时，又怕它突然见底。

与此同时，我每天都会刷到很多惊艳的 AI 产品和创意 Demo。顺手收藏，想着以后研究一下，结果收藏夹越来越满，真正做出来的却没几个。

所以我做了一个实验：
让 Airtap 自动寻找值得验证的海外 AI 创意；发现好点子后，先检查 Codex 剩余额度，额度充足就直接调用 Codex 把它做成 Demo。

结果，它真的交付了一个完整可玩的小游戏。
整个过程中，我没有守在电脑前，只通过 iMessage 发了几条指令。

这就是最后做出来的效果👇
items.title: 用 Airtap 扫创意 + 按 Codex 额度自动出 Demo，离线指令也能交付小游戏
items.summary: 作者痛点是 Codex 额度焦虑（闲置浪费 vs 关键活见底）以及收藏夹堆满 AI Demo 却很少真正做出来。于是做实验：让 Airtap 自动找值得验证的海外 AI 创意；发现点子后检查 Codex 剩余额度，额度够就直接调 Codex 做成 Demo。结果交付了一款完整可玩小游戏，全程不必守在电脑前，只需通过 iMessage 发几条指令。
items.recommend_reason: 把“额度管理 + 创意筛选 + 无人值守交付”串成一条可复制的 agent 流水线。
